q: Who took charge as the Chief of Defence Staff in May 2026?
e: General N. S. Raja Subramani became the third CDS on 31 May 2026; General Dhiraj Seth took over as Army chief on 30 June.

q: Who was appointed Chief of the Air Staff in October 2026?
o: Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh
Air Chief Marshal V. R. Chaudhari
Air Marshal R. K. S. Bhadauria
e: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit took charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 31 October 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh.

q: Who is the Chief of the Naval Staff, who took charge on 31 May 2026?
e: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan took over as the 27th Chief of the Naval Staff on 31 May 2026, the same day as the new CDS.

q: Who is the Chief of the Army Staff of India?
e: General Dhiraj Seth took charge as the 31st Chief of the Army Staff on 30 June 2026.

q: Who is the Chief Justice of India?
e: Justice Surya Kant is the 53rd Chief Justice of India, having taken office in November 2025.

q: Who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
e: Sanjay Malhotra is the 26th Governor of the RBI and chairs the Monetary Policy Committee.

q: Who is the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
e: Gyanesh Kumar is the 26th Chief Election Commissioner. The Election Commission conducts elections to Parliament, State legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.

q: The Sixteenth Finance Commission, whose recommendations were accepted in the 2026-27 Budget, is chaired by:
e: Arvind Panagariya chairs the Sixteenth Finance Commission, which recommended retaining the States' vertical share of central taxes at 41 per cent.

q: In the 2026 Assembly elections, who became the first Bharatiya Janata Party Chief Minister of West Bengal?
e: Suvendu Adhikari was sworn in on 9 May 2026 after the BJP won 207 of the 294 seats, ending Trinamool Congress rule since 2011.

q: Who became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu in May 2026?
e: Actor-politician C. Joseph Vijay of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam was sworn in on 10 May 2026 after his party won 108 seats in the 234-member Assembly.

q: The 2026 Assembly elections were held in four States and one Union Territory. Which of the following was NOT among them?
e: Elections in 2026 were held in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Assam, and in Puducherry. Karnataka was not among them.

q: In Kerala, the 2026 Assembly election produced a change of government in favour of:
e: The Congress-led United Democratic Front won the 2026 Kerala election, dislodging the Left Democratic Front.

q: Himanta Biswa Sarma's return as Chief Minister of Assam in 2026 was notable because he became:
o: the youngest Chief Minister of the State
the first non-Congress leader to return for a second consecutive term
the first Chief Minister to be elected unopposed
the first Chief Minister from the Barak Valley
e: He was sworn in for a second consecutive term on 12 May 2026, the first non-Congress Chief Minister in Assam to do so.

q: Census 2027 will be conducted under which statute?
o: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
e: The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948, with rules framed under it; the Census (Amendment) Rules, 2026 widened who may be appointed an enumerator.

q: The reference date, or census moment, for Census 2027 is:
e: 1 March 2027 is the reference date for the whole country, except Ladakh and snow-bound areas, where it is 1 October 2026.

q: The mascots unveiled for Census 2027 are:
e: 'Pragati' (female) and 'Vikas' (male) were unveiled as mascots, symbolising equal participation of women and men.

q: Caste enumeration in Census 2027 was decided by:
o: the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs
e: The decision was taken by the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs on 30 April 2025; caste will be enumerated in the second phase.

q: Census 2027 will be India's first census conducted:
o: by digital means, with an option of self-enumeration
e: It is the first digital census, with a 15-day self-enumeration window preceding the house-to-house listing phase.

q: The GST Council is a constitutional body created by which amendment?
e: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 inserted Article 279A, creating the GST Council and enabling GST from 1 July 2017.

q: Who is the Vice-President of India?
e: C. P. Radhakrishnan took office as Vice-President in September 2025, succeeding Jagdeep Dhankhar.

q: At its meeting in October 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to:
e: The 63rd MPC meeting, held from 5 to 7 October 2026, raised the repo rate to 5.50 per cent - the first increase in nearly four years.

q: What stance did the Monetary Policy Committee adopt in October 2026?
e: The Committee changed its stance to 'calibrated tightening', having previously held a neutral stance.

q: Following the October 2026 decision, the Standing Deposit Facility rate stands at:
e: The SDF rate is set 25 basis points below the repo rate, at 5.25 per cent, while the MSF rate and Bank Rate stand at 5.75 per cent.

q: Real GDP growth in the first quarter of 2026-27, as estimated by the National Statistical Office, was:
e: Q1 of 2026-27 recorded 7.8 per cent growth, higher than expected, as noted in the October 2026 monetary policy statement.

q: In October 2026 the RBI projected GDP growth for 2026-27 at:
e: The projection for 2026-27 was raised to 7.1 per cent, reflecting strong net exports, government consumption and investment.

q: India's foreign exchange reserves stood at approximately which level in early October 2026?
e: Reserves were about USD 734.6 billion as on 2 October 2026, having peaked at about USD 785.7 billion in early September.

q: The fiscal deficit in the Budget Estimates for 2026-27 was placed at:
e: The fiscal deficit was estimated at 4.3 per cent of GDP for 2026-27, against 4.4 per cent in the Revised Estimates for 2025-26.

q: Public capital expenditure in the 2026-27 Budget was raised to:
e: Public capex was increased to Rs. 12.2 lakh crore for FY 2026-27, from Rs. 11.2 lakh crore in the 2025-26 Budget Estimates.

q: The debt-to-GDP ratio estimated in the 2026-27 Budget, against which the government has set a glide path, is:
e: Debt was estimated at 55.6 per cent of GDP for 2026-27, with a target of 50 plus or minus 1 per cent by 2030-31.

q: The 2026-27 Budget retained the States' vertical share of central taxes at:
e: On the Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendation, the vertical devolution share was retained at 41 per cent.

q: Which of the following was among the seven High-Speed Rail corridors announced in the 2026-27 Budget?
e: The seven 'growth connectors' were Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Bengaluru, Hyderabad-Chennai, Chennai-Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri.

q: NW-5, the first of twenty new National Waterways to be operationalised, is in:
e: NW-5 in Odisha will connect the Talcher and Angul mineral belt and Kalinga Nagar to the ports of Paradip and Dhamra.

q: At its 57th meeting in October 2026, the GST Council recommended:
o: a reduction in the number of tax slabs
the withdrawal of the power to arrest under GST
an increase in the general penalty
the merger of CGST and SGST laws
e: The Council recommended omission of section 69 of the CGST Act, removing arrest powers, and left the rate structure unchanged.

q: The monetary threshold for launching prosecution under GST was raised to:
e: The threshold was raised from Rs. 1 crore to Rs. 5 crore at the 57th GST Council meeting.

q: The general penalty under section 125 of the CGST Act was reduced from Rs. 25,000 to:
e: The maximum general penalty was reduced to Rs. 10,000, and no notice is to be issued where the tax involved is Rs. 10,000 or less.

q: The GST Council decided that changes to GST rates would be considered:
e: The Council said rate changes would be considered once a year, having left the existing rate structure unchanged in October 2026.

q: The time allowed for acknowledging a GST refund claim was reduced from 15 days to:
e: The period for acknowledging refund claims was cut to 10 days, one of several trade-facilitation measures at the 57th meeting.

q: The Union Budget 2026-27 was the first Budget prepared in:
e: It was the first Budget prepared in Kartavya Bhawan, the new secretariat complex that also houses the PMO.

q: India's coastal shipping and inland waterways share of cargo movement is to be raised from 6 per cent to 12 per cent by:
e: The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme aims to raise the share from 6 per cent to 12 per cent by 2047.

q: The Union Budget for 2026-27 was presented on 1 February 2026 by:
e: Nirmala Sitharaman, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, presented the Budget.

q: The 18th BRICS Summit was held in September 2026 at:
e: India hosted the 18th Summit at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on 12 and 13 September 2026, under its 2026 chairship.

q: India's BRICS chairship in 2026 was its:
e: India assumed the chairship on 1 January 2026, succeeding Brazil, for the fourth time after 2012, 2016 and 2021.

q: The theme of India's BRICS chairship in 2026 was:
o: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development
Partnership for Global Development and Security
Towards a Fair and Equitable World Order
e: The theme's four words - resilience, innovation, cooperation, sustainability - were treated as the four pillars of the presidency.

q: The 2026 BRICS Summit concluded with the adoption of the:
e: The New Delhi Declaration was adopted at the close of the summit, covering governance reform, trade, payments and development finance.

q: COP31, the UN climate conference of 2026, is being held from 9 to 20 November 2026 in:
e: COP31 is being held in Antalya, Turkiye; the previous three conferences were held in Dubai (2023), Baku (2024) and Belem (2025).

q: The President of COP31 is:
e: Murat Kurum was nominated President of COP31, while Chris Bowen of Australia is President of Negotiations.

q: Which country is leading the negotiations at COP31, working with Pacific island countries?
e: Australia leads the negotiations, and with Fiji and Tuvalu hosted the pre-COP ministerial meeting in the Pacific in October 2026.

q: The 2026 summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was held in:
e: The 2026 SCO summit was held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, where it was announced that Pakistan would take over the rotating presidency.

q: The President of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly is:
e: Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh presided over the 81st session, which opened in September 2026.

q: Who is the Chair of the United States Federal Reserve?
e: Kevin Warsh took office as Fed Chair in 2026, succeeding Jerome Powell.

q: The President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, who took office in January 2026, is:
e: Zou Jiayi of China succeeded Jin Liqun as President of the AIIB in January 2026.

q: The India AI Impact Summit, held in New Delhi in February 2026, concluded with a declaration endorsed by:
e: The New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact was endorsed by 88 countries and international organisations.

q: The 2026 FIFA World Cup was the first to be hosted by:
e: It was hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico - the first World Cup staged across three countries.

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of BRICS as represented at the 2026 summit?
e: Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the UAE are members alongside Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Nigeria is not.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation?
e: V. Narayanan is Chairman of ISRO and Secretary, Department of Space.

q: GSLV-F18, launched on 30 October 2026, carried which satellite?
e: GSLV-F18 carried NVS-03, a second-generation navigation satellite, restoring the NavIC constellation to four satellites.

q: ISRO's first uncrewed mission under the Gaganyaan programme is intended to:
o: land a rover near the lunar south pole
test the crew module and escape systems before a crewed flight
place a space station module in orbit
study the sun from the L1 point
e: The G1 uncrewed mission tests the crew module, its parachutes and escape systems before Indian astronauts fly.

q: The target year set by India for commissioning the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is:
e: The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted for 2035, with the first module planned by 2028, ahead of a crewed Moon landing by 2040.

q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for:
o: the discovery of light-gated ion channels and optogenetics
the discovery of the hepatitis C virus
e: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel were honoured for optogenetics, which allows individual nerve cells to be switched on or off with light.

q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Francis Halzen for:
o: the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
the invention of the blue LED
e: Halzen was honoured for turning a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into the IceCube detector and for the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.

q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognised work on:
o: non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric synthesis
e: Henri Kagan of France and Kenso Soai of Japan were honoured for explaining how living systems came to contain one of two mirror-image forms of a molecule.

q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to:
e: The Canadian poet and translator Anne Carson was honoured for an oeuvre in dialogue with the classical tradition.

q: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay for:
o: efforts to promote peace and international law
e: Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay, the South African jurist, was honoured for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded for work that produced:
o: New Keynesian models of macroeconomic stabilisation
e: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford were honoured for the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation, used by central banks worldwide.

q: COP31 in Antalya is expected to launch which formal process under the Paris Agreement?
e: The first global stocktake concluded in 2023; COP31 launches the second, which assesses collective progress towards long-term goals.

q: The mascot of COP31 is:
e: Caretta, named for the loggerhead turtle that nests on Antalya's beaches, is the mascot of the conference.

q: The pre-COP ministerial meeting held in October 2026, ahead of COP31, took place in:
o: the Pacific, hosted with Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia
e: Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia partnered to host the official pre-COP and leaders' event in the Pacific in October 2026.

q: According to the United Nations, 2026 was a year in which scientists confirmed that the world is on track to:
o: stay within 1.5 degrees Celsius of pre-industrial levels
exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius warming threshold
e: The UN noted that 2026 saw catastrophic floods, heatwaves and droughts, with the world on track to exceed the 1.5 degree threshold.

q: Which climate phenomenon was expected to intensify impacts in 2026 and into the COP31 period?
e: A powerful El Nino was expected to intensify climate impacts, compounding an already extreme year.

q: The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, the parent treaty of the Paris Agreement, was adopted in:
e: The UNFCCC was adopted in 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit; the Paris Agreement was adopted under it in 2015.

q: The Paris Agreement, under which countries submit nationally determined contributions, was adopted in:
e: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21 in 2015 and entered into force in 2016.

q: The number of Parties to the UNFCCC is:
e: There are 197 Parties to the Convention, which is why COP31 brings together representatives of nearly every country.

q: COP30, held in 2025, took place in:
e: COP30 was held in Belem, Brazil, in the Amazon; COP29 was in Baku and COP28 in Dubai.

q: Which greenhouse gas contributes the largest share of human-caused warming?
e: Carbon dioxide, largely from burning fossil fuels, accounts for the largest share of warming, though methane is far more potent per molecule.

q: The Nobel Prizes were established by the will of Alfred Nobel, drawn up in:
e: Nobel signed his final will in 1895; the first prizes were awarded in 1901, five years after his death.

q: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in:
e: The first awards were made in 1901, in Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace.

q: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded by:
o: the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet
e: Under Nobel's will the Peace Prize is decided by a Norwegian committee and presented in Oslo; the others are decided in Sweden and presented in Stockholm.

q: The Nobel Prize in Literature is awarded by:
o: the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
e: The Swedish Academy awards the Literature prize; the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awards Physics, Chemistry and Economic Sciences.

q: The prize in Economic Sciences differs from the other Nobel Prizes because it:
o: was established in 1968 by Sweden's central bank in memory of Nobel
is awarded only in even years
is decided by the Norwegian Parliament
e: The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel was established in 1968, not by Nobel's will.

q: Each 2026 Nobel Prize carried prize money of:
e: The 2026 prizes were worth 12 million Swedish kronor each, about USD 1.2 million.

q: The Nobel Prizes are presented every year on 10 December, which is:
o: the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death
the founding day of the Nobel Foundation
the day the will was opened
e: The ceremony is held on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death in 1896.

q: Garba of Gujarat was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in:
e: Garba was inscribed in 2023 at the eighteenth session held in Kasane, Botswana, and was then India's fifteenth inscription on the List.

q: Which Indian festival was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2025?
e: Deepavali was inscribed in 2025; Durga Puja in Kolkata was inscribed in 2021.

q: The multinational nomination on henna, listed for examination in the 2026 cycle, was submitted by:
e: Henna: rituals, aesthetic and social practices was submitted by seventeen countries including India, for the Committee's twenty-first session in late 2026.

q: Which country won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026?
e: India beat New Zealand in the final at Ahmedabad on 8 March 2026 to win the title for the third time.

q: India won the 2026 T20 World Cup final by a margin of:
e: India made 255 for 5 and bowled New Zealand out for 159, winning by 96 runs at the Narendra Modi Stadium.

q: India's 2026 T20 World Cup win was notable because India became:
o: the first team to win the title at home and the first to defend it
the first team to win three titles in a row
the youngest team to win the title
the first host nation to lose a final
e: It was India's third T20 world title, and the first time any side had won back-to-back titles and the first win at home.

q: The 2026 Asian Games were held in:
e: The 20th Asian Games were held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, and closed on 4 October 2026.

q: India finished the 2026 Asian Games with 85 medals, which placed it:
e: India finished fourth with 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes, its tally 21 short of the 106 won at Hangzhou.

q: India secured fourth place ahead of Uzbekistan because:
o: the host nation broke the tie
e: Both countries won 21 golds; India's 27 silvers against Uzbekistan's 25 decided the ranking.

q: India's men's hockey team won the 2026 Asian Games gold by defeating:
e: India beat Malaysia 5-1 in the final, retaining the title and securing qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

q: Which country topped the medal table at the 2026 Asian Games?
e: China topped the table with 341 medals, including 169 golds; host Japan was second with 269 medals.

q: The next edition of the Asian Games, in 2030, will be held in:
e: Doha will host the 2030 Asian Games; Riyadh is to host the 2034 edition.

q: The 2026 Winter Olympic Games were held in:
e: The Games ran from 6 to 22 February 2026 across Milan, Cortina d'Ampezzo and surrounding venues in northern Italy.

q: Which country topped the medal table at the 2026 Winter Olympics, setting records for golds and total medals?
e: Norway won 18 golds and 41 medals in all, both records, topping the table for the fourth successive Winter Games.

q: Johannes Hoesflot Klaebo's achievement at the 2026 Winter Games was that he:
o: won six gold medals in cross-country skiing, the most by any athlete at a single Winter Games
became the oldest medallist in Winter Games history
won medals in three different sports
carried the flag at the opening ceremony
e: His six golds were the most by any athlete at one Winter Games, and his sixth was the last medal awarded at the Games.

q: The closing ceremony of the 2026 Winter Olympics was held in:
e: The ceremony was held at the Verona Olympic Arena, a Roman amphitheatre in a city that hosted no sporting events.

q: Which country won the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
e: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time at the New York New Jersey Stadium on 19 July 2026, winning the title for the second time.

q: Who scored the winning goal in the 2026 World Cup final?
e: Substitute Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute, with Nico Williams providing the assist.

q: The 2026 World Cup final was played in an expanded format in which the number of teams and matches were:
e: The tournament was the first with 48 teams and 104 matches, up from 32 teams and 64 matches in previous editions.

q: The PM RAHAT scheme, approved in February 2026, provides:
o: cashless treatment of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for accident victims
e: PM RAHAT provides cashless treatment of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for road accident victims, one of the first decisions taken from Seva Teerth.

q: Seva Teerth, inaugurated in February 2026, houses the:
o: Supreme Court and the Law Commission
Prime Minister's Office, the National Security Council Secretariat and the Cabinet Secretariat
NITI Aayog and the Finance Commission
e: Seva Teerth houses the PMO, the NSCS and the Cabinet Secretariat, along with Kartavya Bhavan 1 and 2.

q: The target for Lakhpati Didis was doubled in 2026 to:
e: Having crossed three crore Lakhpati Didis ahead of schedule, the government doubled the target to six crore by March 2029.

q: The corpus of the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund was doubled in 2026 to:
e: The fund was doubled to Rs. 2 lakh crore to finance post-harvest infrastructure.

q: Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, announced in February 2026, has a corpus of:
e: Fund of Funds 2.0 was set up with a corpus of Rs. 10,000 crore to fund startups through alternative investment funds.

q: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana, approved by the Cabinet, is a centrally sponsored scheme for the period:
e: The scheme runs from 2026-27 to 2030-31, focused on village-level infrastructure and governance.

q: The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme approved in 2026 is intended to:
o: deepen domestic manufacturing of mobile phones and components
e: MPMS supports domestic manufacturing of mobile phones and their components, building on the production-linked approach.

q: The scheme that provides accident victims cashless treatment is administered by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
e: The scheme operates through the road transport ministry's framework for cashless treatment of road accident victims.

q: Which Article of the Constitution is most directly engaged by welfare schemes guaranteeing treatment for accident victims?
e: Article 21, the right to life and personal liberty, has been read to include the right to health care and emergency medical treatment.

q: Kartavya Bhavan, where the Union Budget 2026-27 was prepared, forms part of the:
e: Kartavya Bhavan and Seva Teerth are part of the Central Vista redevelopment in New Delhi.

q: The government's target of a developed India is expressed in the phrase:
e: Viksit Bharat 2047 sets the goal of a developed India by the centenary of Independence.

q: The Lakhpati Didi initiative works primarily through which network?
o: Self-help groups under the rural livelihoods mission
e: The programme works through women's self-help groups under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission.

q: Which of the following is a centrally sponsored scheme rather than a central sector scheme?
e: Centrally sponsored schemes are implemented by States with shared funding; the others are Union government functions.

q: The Ministry of Cooperation, which anchors several 2026 initiatives, was created in:
e: The Ministry of Cooperation was carved out of the Agriculture Ministry in July 2021.

q: Seva Teerth and Kartavya Bhavan were inaugurated in the same month as:
e: Both were inaugurated in February 2026, the month the Budget for 2026-27 was presented.

q: Which of the following best describes the difference between a mission and a scheme in government parlance?
o: Missions are always funded by States
Missions are time-bound programmes with a stated outcome, often spanning several schemes
e: A mission is a time-bound umbrella with a defined outcome, delivered through one or more schemes.

q: The 'Didis' in Lakhpati Didi refers to:
e: The term refers to women in self-help groups who cross an annual income threshold of one lakh rupees.

q: The Direct Benefit Transfer architecture that underpins many welfare schemes relies on:
e: DBT transfers benefits to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts, reducing leakage.

q: Phase I of Noida International Airport was inaugurated in March 2026 at:
e: The airport at Jewar in Uttar Pradesh was inaugurated on 28 March 2026, taking the State to seventeen airports.

q: The Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat corridor was inaugurated in full in February 2026. Its length is:
e: The 82 km Regional Rapid Transit System corridor connects Delhi with Meerut, cutting the journey to under an hour.

q: The Namo Bharat trains on the Delhi-Meerut corridor are designed for a top speed of:
e: The RRTS rolling stock is designed for 180 km per hour, though services run at lower operational speeds.

q: What was notable about the Meerut launch in February 2026?
o: It was India's first metro in a city without a railway station
Namo Bharat and Metro services began from a single platform and shared track
It was India's first driverless metro
It was the first metro to run entirely on solar power
e: For the first time in India, a rapid rail and a metro service were launched together, running on the same track and station.

q: The Delhi-Meerut RRTS project is financed in part by:
e: The New Development Bank, the BRICS institution, financed the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS.

q: The first Vande Bharat Sleeper service, launched in January 2026, ran between:
e: The first sleeper service ran on the Howrah-Guwahati route, flagged off in January 2026.

q: The Vande Bharat Sleeper service flagged off on 1 November 2026 connects:
e: The SMVT Bengaluru to CSMT Mumbai service was flagged off on 1 November 2026, after the Varanasi-New Delhi run.

q: By March 2026, the share of India's broad-gauge railway network that had been electrified stood at:
e: Electrification reached 99.6 per cent of the broad-gauge network by March 2026, up from about a fifth before 2014.

q: The Modified UDAN scheme launched in 2026 aims to connect:
e: The revamped regional connectivity scheme targets 120 new destinations, building on 665 existing routes.

q: Digi Yatra, the facial-recognition based passenger system, was operational in 2026 at:
e: Digi Yatra was operational at 38 airports by May 2026, having been used by more than nine crore passengers.

q: The Delhi-Dehradun Economic Corridor, completed in 2026, is notable for:
e: The 213 km corridor includes Asia's longest elevated wildlife corridor through an ecologically sensitive zone.

q: The Ahmedabad-Dholera Expressway, opened in 2026, is approximately:
e: The 109 km expressway links Ahmedabad with the Dholera special investment region.

q: The number of operational airports in India rose from 74 in 2014 to which figure in 2026?
e: Operational airports rose from 74 to 165, supported by greenfield projects including Mopa, Kannur, Navi Mumbai and Noida.

q: An MRO facility whose foundation was laid at Jewar in 2026 addresses the fact that a large share of Indian aircraft maintenance is carried out:
e: Most Indian aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul work was being sent abroad; the facility aims to bring it home.

q: Which of the following was the first Namo Bharat corridor to be fully commissioned?
e: Delhi-Meerut was the first RRTS corridor to be completed and opened in full, in February 2026.

q: The Sarai Kale Khan station on the Delhi-Meerut corridor is significant because it integrates:
o: a port and a dry dock
e: Sarai Kale Khan, like Anand Vihar, Ghaziabad and Meerut, integrates railway, metro and bus stands.

q: The Pralay missile, whose user trials concluded in November 2026, is a:
o: quasi-ballistic missile with a range of up to 500 km
e: Pralay is a solid-fuelled quasi-ballistic missile with a range of up to 500 km that can manoeuvre in flight to evade defences.

q: The Pralay user trial of November 2026 was conducted from:
o: Wheeler Island, now Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island
e: The launch took place from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast, with range instruments at Chandipur tracking it.

q: Pralay is developed by which organisation?
e: Pralay has been developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation.

q: Exercise MILAN 2026, hosted by the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam, was accompanied by:
e: MILAN 2026 was held alongside an International Fleet Review at Visakhapatnam in February 2026, with 74 nations taking part.

q: The International Fleet Review held in February 2026 was India's:
e: India had held fleet reviews in 2001 and 2016; the 2026 review at Visakhapatnam was the third.

q: Exercise PRAGATI 2026, held at Umroi in Meghalaya, was a maiden exercise involving:
o: armies of Indian Ocean Region countries
e: PRAGATI 2026 was the first table-top and field training exercise among armies of Indian Ocean Region countries.

q: Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026, the second edition of India's multinational air exercise, was held at:
e: The second edition was held at Jodhpur with the theme 'Power in Partnership'.

q: Exercise Yudh Abhyas is conducted between India and:
e: Yudh Abhyas is the India-United States army exercise; its 22nd edition was held in 2026.

q: INS Nipun, commissioned in 2026, belongs to which class of vessels?
e: INS Nipun is the second of the Nistar-class diving support vessels, commissioned at Mumbai.

q: India took over the chairmanship of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium for the term:
e: India assumed the IONS chairmanship for 2026-28, sixteen years after hosting the forum.

q: The Defence Acquisition Council cleared in 2026 the construction of Project 18A:
e: Project 18A covers next-generation destroyers displacing more than 10,000 tonnes, alongside eight new corvettes.

q: Agni-4, tested in August 2026, is a:
e: Agni-4 is a medium-range ballistic missile, test-fired from the Odisha coast in August 2026.

q: Which of the following is the highest peacetime gallantry award of India?
e: The Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award; the Param Vir Chakra is awarded for wartime gallantry.

q: The Chief of Defence Staff is also:
o: Secretary, Department of Military Affairs, and Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee
Chairman of the National Security Council
the senior-most judge of the Armed Forces Tribunal
head of the Defence Research and Development Organisation
e: The CDS is Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs and Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.

q: The Integrated Theatre Commands proposed for the Indian armed forces are intended to:
o: merge the three services into one
bring forces of different services in a geographical or functional theatre under a single commander
e: Theatre commands place army, navy and air force elements in a theatre under one commander to improve jointness.

q: Exercise Pitch Black, in which India has participated, is hosted by:
e: Pitch Black is a multinational air exercise hosted by Australia, in which the Indian Air Force has taken part.

q: In August 2026 a nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court delivered a judgment on the definition of 'industry'. The statute in question was the:
e: The reference concerned the definition of 'industry' under section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

q: The 1978 'triple test' referred to in that judgment comes from which case?
o: Bangalore Water Supply v A. Rajappa
S.P. Gupta v Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
e: The triple test was laid down in Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v A. Rajappa (1978).

q: In Vanashakti v Union of India (2026) the Supreme Court held that:
o: prior environmental clearance remains the rule, and a one-time exemption for existing projects does not become permanent
environmental clearance is unnecessary for all infrastructure projects
the Environment Protection Act is unconstitutional
States may grant clearances in place of the Centre
e: The Court quashed the 2021 office memorandum that had extended the one-time exemption indefinitely.

q: In Jaya Thakur v Union of India (2026) the Supreme Court linked menstrual health to:
e: The Court read menstrual health into the rights to life, health and education under Articles 21 and 21A.

q: In Harish Rana v Union of India (2026) the Court held that clinically assisted nutrition is:
o: medical treatment, relevant to decisions on passive euthanasia
e: The Court treated clinically assisted nutrition as medical treatment, which can be refused under the passive euthanasia framework.

q: Hamsaanandini Nanduri v Union of India (2026) concerned maternity benefit for:
e: The Court read down section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020 to extend 12 weeks' maternity benefit to adoptive mothers.

q: In Chinthada Anand (2026) the Supreme Court held that a person who converts to Christianity:
o: must be treated as a minority
e: The Court held that conversion to Christianity removes eligibility for Scheduled Caste status, following settled law.

q: In 2026 the Supreme Court upheld the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision in:
e: The Court upheld the Bihar special intensive revision of electoral rolls in the 2026 challenge brought by the Association for Democratic Reforms.

q: Padam Mehta v Union of India (2026) concerned:
o: the right to receive education in one's mother tongue
the right to privacy in schools
e: The Court connected mother tongue education with the freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

q: In October 2026 the Supreme Court held that the right to access the internet forms part of:
e: The Court located internet access in the right to life read with the freedom of speech, in a case concerning child sexual abuse material.

q: A judgment delivered by a nine-judge bench is significant because such benches are constituted to decide:
o: questions of law of unusual constitutional importance
e: Larger benches are constituted when a question requires reconsideration of precedent or involves a major constitutional issue.

q: Under Article 145 of the Constitution, the minimum number of judges required to decide a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution is:
e: Article 145(3) requires a bench of at least five judges for such questions, unless the Court provides otherwise.

q: The Code on Social Security, 2020, interpreted in the adoptive mothers' case, is one of:
e: The four labour codes are those on wages, industrial relations, social security, and occupational safety.

q: The doctrine that a law must be both substantively and procedurally fair, central to the 2026 health rights judgments, derives from:
o: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
A.K. Gopalan v State of Madras
Shankari Prasad v Union of India
e: Maneka Gandhi (1978) held that procedure under Article 21 must be fair, just and reasonable.

q: The Supreme Court's power to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights is conferred by:
e: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court; Article 226 gives High Courts a parallel power, wider in scope.

q: A 'special leave petition' is filed under:
e: Article 136 confers discretionary special leave to appeal to the Supreme Court from any court or tribunal.

q: The 2026 Commonwealth Games were held in:
e: Glasgow hosted the Games from 23 July to 2 August 2026, with 74 nations and 11 sports.

q: India finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with 39 medals and a rank of:
e: India finished fourth with 13 golds, 17 silvers and 9 bronzes, its second successive fourth place.

q: India finished ahead of Scotland in 2026 despite both winning 39 medals because:
o: the host nation broke the tie
e: Both had 13 golds; India's 17 silvers against Scotland's 9 decided the order.

q: Which contingent contributed the most medals to India's 2026 Commonwealth Games tally?
e: Boxing contributed ten medals, including seven golds, the largest share of India's haul.

q: Which country topped the 2026 Commonwealth Games medal table for a record fifteenth time?
e: Australia topped the table with 171 medals, including 70 golds.

q: Mirabai Chanu's 2026 Commonwealth Games gold was notable because it was her:
o: third consecutive Commonwealth gold in weightlifting
first medal in a heavier category
only medal of the Games for India
e: She won a third successive Commonwealth gold in weightlifting, in the women's 48 kg category.

q: Neeraj Chopra's medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games was:
e: Chopra won silver in the men's javelin throw at Glasgow 2026.

q: The 2030 Commonwealth Games, the centenary edition, are to be held in:
e: Ahmedabad was chosen to host the 2030 centenary Commonwealth Games.

q: The first Commonwealth Games were held in 1930 in:
e: The first edition, then called the British Empire Games, was held at Hamilton, Canada, in 1930.

q: India won the 2026 Indian Premier League title. The champions were:
e: RCB beat Gujarat Titans by five wickets in the final at Ahmedabad on 31 May 2026, their second consecutive title.

q: The 2026 IPL final was played at:
e: The final was held at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, on 31 May 2026.

q: Which batter finished the 2026 IPL as the highest run-scorer and most valuable player?
e: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi of Rajasthan Royals topped the run chart and was named most valuable player.

q: The 2026 IPL was the tournament's:
e: The 2026 season was the 19th edition of the IPL, with ten teams and 74 matches.

q: India's representation at the 2026 Winter Olympics consisted of:
o: two athletes, who won no medal
four athletes, who won a bronze
six athletes, who won no medal
e: India sent two athletes, an alpine skier and a cross-country skier, and has never won a Winter Olympic medal.

q: The Khelo India Winter Games 2026 were held in:
e: The 2026 edition was held at Gulmarg in Jammu and Kashmir and Leh in Ladakh, with the Indian Army topping the table.

q: India won its first Women's Cricket World Cup in 2025 by defeating:
e: India beat South Africa in the final at Navi Mumbai in November 2025 to win its first Women's World Cup.

q: The Union Budget for 2026-27 raised the railway capital expenditure to which level?
e: Railway budgetary support rose to Rs. 2.78 lakh crore for 2026-27, nearly nine times the 2014-15 level.

q: The foundation stone of a major semiconductor fabrication facility was laid in 2026 at:
e: A semiconductor factory was announced for Noida in western Uttar Pradesh, part of the India Semiconductor Mission.

q: The India Semiconductor Mission's second phase, ISM 2.0, announced in the 2026-27 Budget, focuses on:
o: equipment, materials and full-stack Indian design
e: ISM 2.0 targets equipment and materials, full-stack Indian IP and supply-chain resilience.

q: Dedicated Rare Earth Corridors announced in the 2026-27 Budget are to support which States?
o: Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
e: The corridors are intended to help mineral-rich Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

q: The coastal cargo share target set in the 2026-27 Budget is to rise from 6 per cent to 12 per cent by:
e: The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme aims to double the share by 2047.

q: The new Dedicated Freight Corridor announced in the 2026-27 Budget connects:
o: Dankuni in the east to Surat in the west
e: The corridor links Dankuni in the east with Surat in the west, adding to the existing freight corridor network.

q: Which of the following best describes a 'safe harbour' provision, referred to in the 2026-27 Budget for IT services?
o: A rule protecting firms from tax scrutiny if they accept a specified margin
e: Safe harbour allows a taxpayer accepting a prescribed margin to avoid detailed transfer-pricing scrutiny; the threshold was raised in 2026-27.

q: Which body decides the policy repo rate in India?
o: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI
The Securities and Exchange Board of India
e: The six-member Monetary Policy Committee, chaired by the RBI Governor, sets the policy repo rate.

q: India's GST is best described as a tax on:
e: GST is a destination-based tax on consumption, levied on the supply of goods and services.

q: Which institution is the custodian of India's foreign exchange reserves?
o: The Securities and Exchange Board of India
e: The RBI holds and manages the foreign exchange reserves, publishing the position weekly.

q: The motto of the Olympic Games, 'Citius, Altius, Fortius', translates as:
e: The Latin motto means Faster, Higher, Stronger, and was introduced at the suggestion of Pierre de Coubertin.

q: The next Summer Olympic Games, in 2028, will be held in:
e: Los Angeles hosts the 2028 Games; Brisbane hosts in 2032.

q: National Sports Day in India is observed on 29 August in memory of:
e: The day marks the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

q: The Khelo India programme, under which the Winter Games are held, was launched in:
e: Khelo India was launched in 2018 to revive grassroots sports and identify talent.

q: The Constitution's directive to the State to raise the level of nutrition and public health appears in:
e: Article 47 directs the State to raise nutrition and public health and to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs.

q: The 'basic structure' doctrine, often invoked in Constitution Bench cases, was laid down in:
o: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v Union of India
Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain
e: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

q: The Preamble to the Constitution describes India as a:
e: The Preamble, as amended in 1976, describes India as a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic.

q: Which of the following pairs of sport and its national federation's parent body is correct?
o: Cricket - BCCI, affiliated to the ICC
Hockey - HI, affiliated to the ICC
Athletics - AFI, affiliated to the BCCI
e: The BCCI is affiliated to the International Cricket Council; hockey is affiliated to the FIH and athletics to World Athletics.
